summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 12, part 20) in which Charles Houseman writes a farewell letter saying he is sailing that night and will be away about six weeks, asking that Mrs. Enderby's daughter be told he will hold his tongue and never bother her again. The next morning Lexy and Mrs. Enderby talk at breakfast: no letter has arrived, Mrs. Enderby will tell Mr. Enderby that evening, and Lexy announces she is going to Wyngate to look for Caroline. Mrs. Enderby insists no such person has arrived in Wyngate and that Lexy is chasing a mystery that does not exist.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, Charles Houseman sails away after a farewell letter, and Lexy defies Mrs. Enderby to search for Caroline in Wyngate.
key_facts: Charles Houseman's letter is signed from the company's office, J. J. Eames & Son, 99 State Street.
Charles Houseman writes that the company's ship is sailing to-night and that he expects to be back in about six weeks.
Charles Houseman promises to hold his tongue and never to bother Mrs. Enderby's daughter again in any way.
Lexy cries 'Then he's gone! He's gone!' upon hearing that Charles Houseman is sailing.
The breakfast conversation takes place the morning after the letter, with Mr. Enderby already gone to his office.
Mrs. Enderby says she will tell Mr. Enderby 'This evening' and will then be 'guided by his advice'.
Lexy privately doubts that Mrs. Enderby is likely to be guided by her husband, but keeps the thought to herself.
Mrs. Enderby tells Lexy that there is no mystery and that Lexy wishes to amuse herself with a grand mystery.
Lexy says her trunk is packed and she will send for it that afternoon.
Lexy announces she is going to Wyngate, a small village the two passed through on the way to Miss Craigie's house.
Mrs. Enderby says she made certain inquiries and that no such person as Caroline has arrived in Wyngate.
Mrs. Enderby describes Lexy's thoughts, predicting she will go to Wyngate and discover that Mrs. Enderby is wrong.
